    """Convert a Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M with subtractive pairs) to an integer."""

    }
    total = 0
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:

        cur_val = values[s[i]]
        # Look ahead to see if next symbol forms a subtractive pair
        if i + 1 < n:

            if cur_val < next_val:

def camel_to_snake(s: str) -> str:
    """Convert camelCase or PascalCase to snake_case.
    Consecutive capitals stay together (HTTPServer -> http_server)."""
    if not s:
        return s
    result = []
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        c = s[i]
        if c.isupper():
            # start of a word; find end of consecutive capitals
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and s[j].isupper():
                j += 1
            # If next char is lowercase, this is a boundary between acronym and word
            if j < n and s[j].islower():
                # keep all but last capital in current word
                if i < j - 1:
                    result.append(s[i:j-1].lower())
                result.append('_')
                result.append(s[j-1].lower())
                i = j
            else:
                # all caps word
                result.append(s[i:j].lower())
                i = j
        else:
            result.append(c)
            i += 1
    # Join and replace possible leading underscore
    snake = "".join(result)
    # Remove leading underscore if present
    if snake.startswith('_'):
        snake = snake[1:]
    return snake
